claim: For the Gaussian droplet-survival kernel \(\phi_b(t)=\exp(-\pi t^2/(4b^2))\), with \(b>0\), let \(g(t)=\sum_{j=1}^{m} a_j e^{-\lambda_j t}\) be any finite positive exponential mixture with \(a_j>0\), \(\lambda_j\ge0\), and \(\sum_{j=1}^{m}a_j=1\). For every \(T>0\), its uniform log-error \(E_T(g)=\sup_{0\le t\le T}|\log(g(t)/\phi_b(t))|\) obeys \[E_T(g)\ge \frac{\pi T^2}{24b^2}.\] Consequently, \(\sup_{0\le t\le T}|g(t)/\phi_b(t)-1|\ge 1-\exp(-\pi T^2/(24b^2))\). The bound is independent of the number and rates of the exponential terms; it concerns uniform relative/log accuracy, not absolute error or general state-space realizations.

scientific.integrity: The bound is proved analytically by log-convexity of a finite positive exponential mixture and a midpoint inequality; no finite experiment is used as proof.
limitations: Applies only to finite positive exponential mixtures normalized at t=0.
Controls uniform log/relative error, not absolute error.
Does not cover signed sums or arbitrary finite-dimensional state-space realizations.
The lower-bound constant is not claimed to be optimal.
Priority beyond the searched literature is not independently certified.

title: A horizon-dependent log-error floor for positive exponential approximations of a Gaussian survival kernel
